system.description:
You don't build new things — you make old things briefly extraordinary.

  • A sword becomes flame for an hour.
  • A cloak becomes a wing.
  • Everything reverts eventually.
  • Infusers alone among Artificers are trained to work fine enchantment even through a full suit of plate — you are trained in all armour and shields.
  • You also choose one weapon at character creation to gain proficiency in, on top of your normal class weapon list — most Infusers pick whatever they intend to keep permanently enchanted.
  • Infuse Item (1st): As an action, spend 1 Ingenuity Point to grant a mundane weapon, suit of armour, shield, or tool a temporary magical property from your known list (see Known options in The Artificer's Workshop) for 1 hour per level. Number of items infused at once equals half your level (rounded up).
  • Sustained Working (3rd): Infusions no longer end early if you're knocked unconscious — only duration or Ingenuity spent to cancel ends them.
  • Layered Infusion (5th): Infuse a single item with two properties simultaneously for double the Ingenuity cost.
  • Reflexive Infusion (7th): For 1 extra Ingenuity Point, infuse an item as part of another action rather than using your whole action.
  • Lasting Work: Permanent Infusion (10th): As often as Lasting Work allows, spend a full day and appropriate materials to make one infusion permanent on a single item rather than temporary — for example, a blade that keeps Flametongue's fire damage forever, or a shield permanently etched with Ward-Etched's save bonus. The item becomes a true magic item and no longer draws on your Ingenuity Points.
  • Magnum Opus: The Everwork (24th): Create a single permanent magic item embodying every infusion property you know simultaneously. Requires a month of uninterrupted work and rare materials the GM determines. Unique — only one Everwork can exist per Artificer.

Known Infusions

  • Flametongue — Weapon deals an additional 1d6 fire damage on a hit
  • Frostbrand — Weapon deals an additional 1d6 cold damage on a hit, and the target's speed is halved for 1 round
  • Shockgrip — Weapon deals an additional 1d6 lightning damage on a hit
  • Guardian Plating — Armour grants +2 AC
  • Featherweight — The item's slot cost is halved (round up) for the duration; if worn armour, its Strength requirement is waived
  • Returning Throw — A thrown weapon flies back to your hand immediately after the attack resolves
  • Ward-Etched — A shield adds +1 to all saving throws in addition to its normal AC bonus
  • Glowing Ward — The item sheds light in a 30ft radius, and its wielder gains Advantage on saves vs fear
  • Silent Step — Armour or boots grant Advantage on Move Silently checks
  • Bloodhound's Edge — A weapon grants Advantage on checks to track a creature it has damaged within the last 24 hours
  • Reach Extended — A melee weapon's reach increases by 5ft
  • Truth-Etched — A tool grants Advantage on checks to detect forgeries, lies, or magical disguises while in use
  • Deadweight — A weapon adds +2 damage against a target that is Restrained, Prone, or otherwise immobilised

Designing a Custom Infusion

  • Benchmark: A single Infusion should do roughly one of the following — add a damage die (1d6 of a chosen type), grant a flat +1 or +2 to one specific roll or AC, provide a narrow at-will utility effect (light, minor detection, a movement quirk), or impose a specific condition on a hit (halved speed, Disadvantage on the target's next save). Avoid stacking two of these into one Infusion unless it's the result of Layered Infusion (5th level) or Lasting Work.
